title: Trust Region Continual Learning as an Implicit Meta-Learner
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Regularization-only and replay-only updates either drift or lose track of earlier tasks; a trust-region hybrid keeps updates inside overlapping task optima.
layout: 3 stacked rows, each left-to-right before/after, dashed red trust region in last row
description: Three stacked rows of toy 2-D parameter-space sketches, each showing a before state on the left and an after state on the right, joined by a thick black arrow. Colored translucent ellipses mark low-loss regions for tasks T1 (yellow), T2 (blue) and T3 (green). Row (a) is labeled Elastic Weight Consolidation-based approach. The update arrow from θ to θ' ends in the T1/T2 overlap, but a new T3 ellipse appears and the next step ends in a '?', so the EWC update is uncertain. Row (b) is Generative replay-based approach. The replayed tasks are drawn as tilde T's with shifted ellipses, and the update from θ' lands at θ'' in a T3 overlap with drifted old tasks. Row (c) has no printed label. It adds a dashed red trust region around the old optimum, and the update from θ' to θ'' stays inside the region. The eye goes first to the colored overlapping ellipses and the red dashed boundary.
caption: Illustrations of parameter updates when learning a new task $\mathcal{T}_3$ under different continual-learning strategies. Colored ellipses denote low-loss regions for each task. Dark arrows show the current update direction from $\theta$, gray arrows indicate prior trajectory, and the red dashed region indicates the trust region constraint.
abstract: Continual learning aims to acquire tasks sequentially without catastrophic forgetting, yet standard strategies face a core tradeoff: regularization-based methods (e.g., EWC) can overconstrain updates when task optima are weakly overlapping, while replay-based methods can retain performance but drift due to imperfect replay. We study a hybrid perspective: \emph{trust region continual learning} that combines generative replay with a Fisher-metric trust region constraint. We show that, under local approximations, the resulting update admits a Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) interpretation with a single implicit inner step: replay supplies an old-task gradient signal (query-like), while the Fisher-weighted penalty provides efficient offline curvature shaping (support-like). This yields an emergent meta-learning property in continual learning: the model becomes an initialization that rapidly \emph{re-converges} to prior task optima after each task transition, without explicitly optimizing a bilevel objective that couples inner adaptation with outer meta-updates. Empirically, on task-incremental diffusion image generation and continual diffusion-policy control, trust region continual learning achieves the best final performance and retention, and accelerates early-task recovery compared with EWC, replay, and continual meta-learning baselines.
